query: 2026 Tennessee 9th Congressional District Democratic primary August 6 2026 Justin Pearson vs London Lamar polls endorsements latest news
answer:
Report submitted. The headline finding is that **this primary is already decided** — it was held August 6, 2026, and Justin Pearson won 65.7% to London Lamar's 24.3% (32,092 to 11,870), a 41.4-point margin, carrying all 15 counties including Lamar's home Shelby County by 66.2%–27.8%.

A few things worth flagging for whoever consumes this:

**No polling existed.** There was never a public Pearson-vs-Lamar head-to-head survey. The only public primary poll in the cycle was a Data for Progress survey from early February 2026 showing Cohen 45–Pearson 44 — of the *old* district, against the *then-incumbent*, before redistricting. Any secondary source citing "polling" in this race traces back to that.

**Two numeric discrepancies you may encounter.** AP's figures at call time were 64.9%/24.9% (a mid-count snapshot); the completed count is 65.7%/24.3%. And Ballotpedia lists a Democratic total of 46,525 against the TN Secretary of State's 48,811 — I could not reconcile these, but the state feed with all 15 counties complete is the better-supported figure. Results remain formally unofficial until county certification on **August 24, 2026**.

**Structural cause of the blowout.** Pearson entered in October 2025 as a challenger to Cohen and had a seven-month fundraising and organizing head start; Lamar only qualified after the May 2026 redistricting. Final gap: $2.34M to $76K, roughly 31-to-1. The endorsement split was a clean establishment/insurgent divide — Cohen, both mayors, and Harold Ford Sr. for Lamar; Sanders, AOC, SEIU, and AFSCME for Pearson — and the insurgent side won by 41 points.

If the underlying forecasting question concerns the **general** election rather than the primary, the relevant facts are in section 6: Pearson faces Trump-endorsed Brent Taylor on November 3 in a district rated Solid/Safe Republican (Cook PVI R+9, Trump +22 on the new lines), though the DCCC added TN-09 to its target list on August 5. I was unable to retrieve live prediction-market pricing for that contest through the available tooling.

key_facts: The 2026 TN-9 Democratic primary ALREADY OCCURRED on August 6, 2026. Justin J. Pearson won decisively; the question is resolved.

Final unofficial results (15/15 counties, all precincts): Pearson 32,092 (65.7%), London Lamar 11,870 (24.3%), M. LaTroy A-Williams 3,318 (6.8%), Jim Torino 1,531 (3.1%). Total 48,811 votes. Margin 41.4 points.
AP called the Democratic race for Pearson at 8:33 p.m. CDT on August 6, 2026; the Republican race for Brent Taylor at 8:40 p.m. CDT.

Reported-figure discrepancy: Washington Examiner cited AP at 64.9%-24.9% (40-pt margin), likely a mid-count snapshot; NBC News and TN SoS both settled at 65.7%/24.3%. Ballotpedia lists a Democratic total of 46,525 vs. the TN SoS-derived 48,811.
Pearson won all 15 counties in the district, including Shelby County (Memphis) with 19,209 votes / 66.2% to Lamar's 8,049 / 27.8% — beating her ~2.4-to-1 in her home county.
Republican primary: Brent Taylor 46.0% (23,000+ votes), Todd Warner 26.3%, Jeremy Thompson 20.0%, Charlotte Bergmann ~7.7%. Total 64,816 votes — about 16,000 more than the Democratic primary.

NO public head-to-head poll of Pearson vs. Lamar was ever released. The only public primary poll in the cycle was Data for Progress (for Justice Democrats), fielded Jan 30-Feb 3, 2026, of the OLD district: Cohen 45% - Pearson 44%.
Polymarket priced Pearson at 93.4% on July 19, 2026 and 97.2% by primary day (~$20.6K volume). Earlier in the cycle, pre-redistricting, markets had incumbent Cohen at ~58%.

Pearson endorsements: Bernie Sanders, Ed Markey, AOC, Ayanna Pressley, Summer Lee, Ro Khanna, Maxwell Frost, Ilhan Omar; SEIU, AFSCME, Working Families Party, Justice Democrats, Leaders We Deserve, Brady Campaign, Indivisible Action, Memphis For All, Shelby County Young Democrats.

Lamar endorsements: retiring Rep. Steve Cohen, Memphis Mayor Paul Young, Shelby County Mayor Lee Harris, former Rep. Harold Ford Sr., former Mayor A C Wharton, state Sen. Raumesh Akbari, state Rep. Larry Miller, Rep. LaMonica McIver (D-NJ).

AOC, Pressley and Summer Lee headlined a Pearson rally of ~1,000 people at New Direction Church in Memphis on July 17, 2026 — the first day of early voting. Lamar held a competing kickoff with Cohen near Overton Park the same day.

Fundraising was lopsided: Pearson raised $2,344,947 (spent $1,500,214; $844,733 cash on hand; ~55,000 individual donors) vs. Lamar's $76,320 — roughly 31-to-1. Pearson launched in October 2025 against Cohen, giving him a seven-month head start; Lamar only entered after redistricting in May 2026.

Redistricting: following SCOTUS's Louisiana v. Callais weakening VRA Section 2, Gov. Bill Lee called a special session; the map passed May 6 and was signed May 7, 2026, splitting Memphis/Shelby County among TN-5, TN-8 and TN-9 to target a 9R-0D delegation. The filing deadline moved from March 10 to May 15, 2026.

The old TN-9 was 60.2% Black; the new TN-9 is ~31% Black. It is an L-shaped 15-county district running ~200 miles east from the Memphis airport along the southern border, then north to Williamson County and Columbia.
Rep. Steve Cohen (D), who held the seat since 2007 and won 71.3% in 2024, announced on May 15, 2026 he would not seek reelection in any of the three carved-up districts, and endorsed Lamar.

Litigation: Sherman v. Hargett (ACLU/ACLU-TN), filed May 11, 2026. A TRO was denied May 26; a three-judge panel denied a preliminary injunction on July 23, 2026, finding plaintiffs unlikely to succeed on the merits. Underlying claims remain pending; the map governs both the primary and the general.
General election November 3, 2026: Justin Pearson (D) vs. Brent Taylor (R), plus independents Dennis Jeffrey Clark and Michelle Head.

Race ratings as of August 18, 2026: Cook Political Report Solid Republican (PVI R+9); Inside Elections Solid Republican (baseline R+15); Sabato's Crystal Ball Safe Republican; Decision Desk HQ Likely Republican. Trump carried the new lines 60%-38% in 2024.

The DCCC added TN-09 to its 'Districts in Play' offensive target list on Wednesday, August 5, 2026 — the day before the primary — as part of a 12-district expansion bringing its total to 58 targets. Chair Suzan DelBene congratulated Pearson on August 7.
Brent Taylor was endorsed by President Trump (July 13, 2026), Sen. Marsha Blackburn and Sen. Bill Hagerty. He raised $1,549,482 including a $1 million personal loan.
